name: Hart Route
beta: Climb the trough past a bolt to a ledge, then go up cracks and a dihedral to a small overhang. Pass the overhang on the left and climb the chimney to a ledge with a tree. The third pitch walks right into a gully to the foot of the friction slab, and the last climbs the face, clipping two bolts, to the top. The summit of the Head is a scramble from there.
overview: One of the most frequently climbed routes on Camelback, a four-pitch outing that works from a trough on the left edge of a giant flake mass up cracks, a chimney and a friction pitch.

current.descent: scramble south and east to summit, then head's standard descent
current.location: In a trough at the left edge of a giant flake mass, 20 ft right of Misgivings

name: Hawk
beta: Climb the east-facing side of the boulder, clipping two bolts, to the top. Descend with the same single-rope rappel used for Energizer.
overview: A short bolted face on the east-facing side of the Energizer boulder, with the same descent as that route.

current.descent: single-rope rappel
current.location: east-facing side of the triangular boulder, opposite Energizer

name: High Exposure Exit
beta: This is an optional extra pitch above the third-pitch belay of The Classic. A party that has had enough, or is worried about weather, can scramble off to the rappel station instead; otherwise it gives you one more fine pitch.
overview: Precarious, airy face moves wander rightward and upward beside a pair of parallel seams, passing three bolts, before a gully leads you back leftward. It is a worthwhile extra pitch for those who want to finish The Classic rather than bail.

current.area_walk_in: Follow Trail 261 about 1.7 miles to a green metal gate, keep right on the switchbacks, and watch for a big patch of prickly pear near the second large switchback, where the faint climbers' path to the wall leaves the trail (roughly 2 miles total).
current.descent: three rappels via the Coke Bottle route, on the buttress's eastern flank
current.detailed_rack: Bolts, plus a small nut or cam.
current.location: final pitch of The Classic, starting where the Flying Buttress crest joins the main wall

name: Hiliter
beta: Start in the middle of the northeast face and climb straight up past the bolt to the top. For the variation, step off the boulder on the north side onto the northwest face and join the regular route.
overview: A short face climb up the middle of The Wedge's northeast side, protected by a single bolt. An alternate start from a boulder on the north side reaches the same line.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Middle of the northeast face

name: Hippity Hop
beta: Begin at the right end of the lower crag and climb the flared crack into the boulder enclave. Move left across onto the face and go past a bolt to the top.
overview: A short climb on the lower crag that feels like topping out on a small spire. A flared crack leads to a boulder enclave, after which the route crosses left onto the face for the finish.

current.area_walk_in: Head east on the Marcus Landslide trail for roughly a third of a mile, then turn right at the Sven Slab sign. Loop around a big boulder and over a low rise, then pick up the climbers' path on the right toward the Nit Nat flake. Many informal tracks dead-end in brush; if you are squeezing through thick scrub, turn back.
current.descent: short rappel south, or tandem rappel, then scramble through chimney
current.location: Lower crag at the right end of the wall, up and right of Nit Nat

name: I Just Wanna Be in the Guidebook!
beta: Step off the large boulder lying right of the big roof and climb the gentle face, trending slightly left, to the arete. Stay on the face just right of the arete up to the rappel anchor.
overview: A low-angle face climb on the right side of the wall, starting from a boulder beside a big roof and following the face next to an arete up to a rappel anchor.

current.descent: single-line rappel from the anchor, or continue to the top

name: It's Your Party
beta: Climb the slab to a second bolt at an overhang and turn it for the crux. Go on to the bolt where the traverse of E.S.A.D. passes, then take the middle of the face separating those two routes to the top.
overview: A slab route on the main slab between two neighbouring lines. The crux comes at the overhang in the lower half, and the face above eases to a short, steady finish at the anchor.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Jacks Crown
beta: Follow the leftmost bolted line on the long cliff band, beside the gully. The moves ease off the further left you stay.
overview: Pleasant four-bolt line at the left end of a long band; it gets easier the further left you drift.

current.area_walk_in: Walk to the canyon rim from the campground and follow the trail down to the base of the wall; the descent is short, roughly a ten-minute walk.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Leftmost bolt line on the long band beside the gully that divides it from Jack Off's buttress; a stand of trees marks its foot

name: Just Fine
beta: Reach the anchor by crossing the slabs south from close to the summit of Fly By, rappel in, then climb back up the face and the resonant flake or crack, passing two horizontal cracks and two bolts.
overview: Rap in, then climb a face and a resonant flake or crack with two horizontal breaks and two bolts back to the top.

current.area_walk_in: Loose soil and rock below these crags makes walking up damaging and sometimes dangerous, so anchors are placed on top. Gear up above, descend by rope to the base, then climb back up to your packs.
current.descent: Rappel in from the top anchor, then climb back up
current.anchor: rappel anchor reached by crossing slabs from the top of Fly By
current.location: Around 60 ft beyond Fly By; reach the anchor by crossing slabs to the south with a short downclimb

name: Kate's Fault
beta: Begin a bit right of the middle and angle leftward and upward to the center of the face, clipping two bolts and using the xenoliths as holds. Test each hold before trusting it.
overview: A face climb on The Cone that wanders leftward and upward into the middle of the wall with only a couple of bolts. Embedded xenoliths supply many of the holds, and some of them are loose.

current.descent: walk off either end of the wall
current.location: Just right of the center of the wall, angling up and left

name: Lickety Split
beta:
Start in the short crack that arcs rightward and follow it, then ease back left along an indistinct thin crack to a big flake with a crack. Finish the pitch up lichen-covered rock past a horn to a belay bolt.

Climb the face to a bolt, trend upward and rightward to some little ledges that slope down and a second bolt, then move left and follow the obvious water-worn groove up to a crack. Follow that crack up into the large stand of trees at the top.
overview: A bold lead that is hard to find because it has so few bolts; study the wall photo first. The first pitch follows a crack, then an indistinct crack returning leftward to a flake and over lichen-covered rock past a horn to a belay bolt. The second pitch goes via bolts and a conspicuous water-streaked groove up to a crack and the trees at the top.

current.location: Roughly 25 ft along from Hanging Gardens, where a short crack curves rightward

name: Gender Blender
beta: Climb the short face past the bolt, which is where the crux comes, to a small ledge. Then take the wide vertical crack above it to the top.
overview: A short face with a bolt (5.10b) leads to a small ledge and a wide vertical crack, which is followed to the top.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Loafer's Choice
beta: Start at the base of the smooth slab, climb the small dihedral, then carry on up the face, clipping two bolts, to the top.
overview: A quick, worthwhile face climb up a smooth slab that faces east, handy for anyone who does not want to make the longer trip over to The Wedge.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: At the foot of the polished slab that faces east

name: Lord of the Flies
beta: Climb the seam up and leftward, then the face, clipping two bolts, to a horizontal crack. Get onto the big boulder balanced on a ledge and finish up the face, clipping two further bolts.
overview: A seam trending up and left, then face with bolts to a horizontal crack, up and over a large boulder balanced on a ledge, and the easier face above to the top.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: About ten yards beyond Piggys Conch Shell

name: Lose Yer Stance, Shitcher Pants
beta: Climb the bolted face beside the block that sits under Sweet Surprise, on its right. The sequence above the second bolt is where the difficulty lies.
overview: A bolted face line beside Sweet Surprise with a startling sequence above the second bolt; build a gear belay on top.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Lost and Found
beta: Begin on top of the V-shaped lip and climb the face to a bolt, then continue to the left end of a horizontal crack. Move past the crack and finish up the face to the left of the two bolts.
overview: A face route that links a bolt, the left end of a horizontal crack, and a final bolted face to the top of the wall.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Just lower and to the right of Hanging Mantle, starting on a V-shaped lip

name: Climb at First Sting
beta: Go up the steep face lying between Slot and Limbo, clipping three bolts on the way.
overview: A steep face climb named after two scorpions that were living under a loose flake. Whoever placed the lower pair of bolts is not known.

current.area_walk_in: Walk west to the Powerline Trail and follow it about 0.6 mile, then turn onto the Granite Mountain Trail for roughly 0.3 mile. Next take the Granite Mountain Loop Trail around the hill until a climbers' path leads up to the base. About 1.4 miles in total, with a short uphill push at the end.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: On the steep face between Slot and Limbo

name: Lost in the Alps
beta: Begin within a steep corner, and once at its top go rightward and up the bolted face. Later slide leftward round the arete into a corner until you can get back onto the arete, then slant rightward to a crack to sidestep the poorly protected arete.
overview: Corner to bolted face and an arete, stepping off to a crack to dodge the poorly protected edge; easy to toprope.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Begins in a steep corner on the Pharaoh

name: Zig Zag
beta: Start from the boulder at the very bottom of the north face, climb to the highest horizontal crack and follow it left to the base of a crack that arches rightward. Follow it to an alcove with a bolt, then leave leftward and upward to the bulge where a rappel bolt sits.
overview: A zigzagging line on the north face: a horizontal crack leads left, an arching crack leads to an alcove, and a bulge exit finishes the route at a rappel bolt.

current.descent: rappel from a bolt at the bulge

name: High On The Hog
beta: Go up the corner that faces left, clipping two bolts, to a roof, traverse beneath it to the third bolt, then take the thin crack to the top.
overview: A left-facing corner leads by two bolts to a roof. Move under the roof to the third bolt, then take a thin crack to the top.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: about 50 ft along from Pissed Off

name: Mean Streak
beta: Start on the slab facing northeast, directly under Mickey Mantle and climb straight up the face, clipping two bolts, to the top.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: On a slab facing northeast, immediately under Mickey Mantle

name: Mickey Mantle
beta: Start beneath the smooth face to the right of Rurpture and climb past a bolt to join the crack shortly before the corner. Carry on over the little overhang, clipping a bolt, to the top.
overview: A short climb on the AMC Boulder that begins beneath a smooth face, slants into a crack just short of a corner, and finishes over a small overhang.

current.descent: short rappel from the eyebolt on top
current.location: Right of Rurpture, beneath a smooth face

name: Mirror Image
beta: Follow the crack system running up the middle of the face. Protection is scarce low down and becomes better as you gain height.
overview: Follows the crack system up the middle of the face. It sees plenty of traffic, so loose rock should be less of a concern. Gear is thin low down and gets better higher.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.detailed_rack: Standard rack; a big piece (BD #4) may be wanted at the top.
current.location: crack system at the face's centre

name: Made in The Shade
beta: Work up beyond horizontal cracks to a bolted prow, then finish on the face above, clipping two more bolts on the way to the top.

current.area_walk_in: Pick whichever trail seems best, beginning at the wall's left end, and head up. The slope is thick with catclaw, so wear long pants.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: twenty feet right of Duckin' For Jesus and left of Where the Fughowi

name: Won't Get Fooled Again
beta: Go up the trough, passing cracks, to a ledge and a bolt, then face climb through the second bolt to an undercling and the third bolt. Continue straight up the face above to the top.
overview: Follow the trough, passing cracks, to a ledge with a bolt. Face climbing then leads by a second bolt to an undercling and a third bolt, continuing directly overhead to finish.

current.area_walk_in: Pick whichever trail seems best, beginning at the wall's left end, and head up. The slope is thick with catclaw, so wear long pants.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: over Manly Bulges, in the base of a trough

name: Eat Shit And Die
beta: Start where Rest In Peace starts, traverse in from the left, and climb the face, clipping one bolt, into the right-hand crack. Follow that crack to the top.
overview: Traverse in from the left and climb the face past a bolt into the right-hand crack, then follow the crack to the top.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: shares its start with Rest In Peace

name: Home Of The Brave
beta: Climb a short corner to an overhanging flake that you layback, then keep going beyond a single bolt before following crack and face above.
overview: A bold lead for a first ascent. A short right-facing corner leads to a layback flake on an overhang, then the route passes a bolt and continues on crack and face.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: about 20 ft over from E.S.A.D.

name: Mousetrap
beta: On the west face's right edge, one bolt and one pin lead up into a crack system. Where the crack runs out you can either pull over the bulge or escape leftward to Rabbit Tracks.
overview: Bolt and piton protection leads into a crack system, at whose end the bulge can be climbed (5.8 R) or you can step across to Rabbit Tracks.

current.area_walk_in: Circle round the overlook's western flank while hugging the practice cliff; a brief down-climb leads to the overlook's foot, and a trail then bears down and left, passing between boulders.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: extreme right end of the west face

name: Mystical Adventures
beta: Begin ten feet to the right of Banana Crack and climb the face past a bolt to a horizontal crack, and finish exactly as Banana Crack does.
overview: A face climb that heads for a horizontal crack and then merges with Banana Crack for the finish.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: About 3 m right of the Banana Crack start

name: Naked Edge
beta: Start at the right side of the southeast face, go up the slender crack and the face to the corner, then follow the corner to the top. Double ropes are the safeguard against rope damage should a fall swing you round the corner.
overview: A route of slender crack and face on the southeast face that leads to a corner and follows it to the summit. Double ropes help because the rope can be damaged around the corner.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Begins at the right-hand end of the wedge's southeast face

name: Neck Route
beta: On the first pitch climb the loose gully with its minor overhangs, until a rightward traverse leads to a small belay ledge. The second pitch crosses rightward onto the exposed face and go straight up the water chute to a bolt in the gully, then scramble up the gully to the summit.
overview: A two-pitch line from the saddle between the Head and the Hump, using a loose gully and then an exposed face with a water chute. Easy scrambling above reaches the summit of the Head.

current.descent: scramble class 2 gully to the summit, then the head's standard descent
current.location: At the saddle between the Head and the Hump, at the foot of a gully

name: Ways
beta: Start up Swept Away, reaching the stance above the arch, then continue on Ways itself. Tiny wired nuts are useful on the face over the arch.
overview: Follows Swept Away to the arch-top belay, then breaks off on its own finish up a face that takes small brass nuts.

current.location: Climb Swept Away as far as the stance atop the arch

name: Never Never Land
beta: Share the opening with South Gully and follow it until you can traverse left along a horizontal crack to a small ledge under a bolt. Above that, a face with four bolts leads up to the top of the West Summit.
overview: A bold, airy face climb to the West Summit that makes a climber feel alone on the rock. The first ascensionist put in three bolts from stances but had to use hooks for the fourth.

current.area_walk_in: From the trailhead, follow the main park trail and look for the spur marked for climbing access, which leads to the peak from the east. Another way is to take the wide cart path from the visitor center to the first climbers' trail sign, then head up and left toward the peak.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Same start as South Gully

name: Nit Nat
beta: Start twenty feet right of Changes in Latitude beneath a small undercling. Climb the face, clipping three bolts, to a horizontal crack, then carry on up the face above it to the top.
overview: Its first climbers could not decide whether the moves or the gnats were worse. A face with three bolts leads to a horizontal crack, and more face finishes it.

current.area_walk_in: Head east on the Marcus Landslide trail for roughly a third of a mile, then turn right at the Sven Slab sign. Loop around a big boulder and over a low rise, then pick up the climbers' path on the right toward the Nit Nat flake. Many informal tracks dead-end in brush; if you are squeezing through thick scrub, turn back.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Beside Changes in Latitude on its right, under a small undercling

name: No Easy Four
beta: Start on top of the big standing flake in the gully and climb the crack system above to a horizontal crack. Traverse left along it until below a bolt, then work up the face, well right of the pair of bolts.
overview: A crack system leads straight up to a horizontal crack, which is traversed left to a bolt on the face, and the face is climbed to the top.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: About four ft beyond Lost and Found, perched on a tall freestanding flake in the gully

name: Noodler
beta: Follow the line of bolts right of Perspective until it crosses Perspective at an angling crack. A finger-size nut or cam protects the moves through the horizontal crack.
overview: A 70 ft bolt line that cuts across Perspective; a small piece protects the horizontal crack.

current.area_walk_in: Walk past the restrooms and follow the clear path along the ridge, away from the road, to the big pinnacle called Nancy's Thumb. Descend the steep gully beneath it; the routes line the wall to your right.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Bolt line just right of Perspective, crossing it at the slanting crack

name: Otherwise
beta: Begin on the east side and climb the face, clipping two bolts, straight to the top.

current.area_walk_in: Reached by walking up a ramp that runs beside the canyon's right edge.
current.descent: single-rope rappel off the north side
current.location: East side of the pinnacle, straight up the face

name: Pasta Man Unchained
beta: Begin at the right side of the south face and angle leftward up the face, clipping two bolts, to the roof's left end. A single distinctive move takes you over it, and the belay with two bolts is just beyond.
overview: A south-face route on Pasta Slab that angles leftward up a bolted face to a roof. The way over the roof is the part people remember.

current.descent: single-rope rappel to the south over the roof
current.detailed_rack: Small to medium nuts, 2 bolts on the face, and a 2 bolt anchor.
current.location: right side of the south face

name: Pecker Party
beta: Share the start with Birthday Party and follow the ramp rightward until you can climb the face above, clipping two bolts, to a roof. There, cross to the right and meet Dried Oatmeal for the finish.
overview: A short face route that leaves the Birthday Party ramp, climbs to a roof, then crosses right to merge with Dried Oatmeal. The first ascensionists drilled both bolts from stances.

current.area_walk_in: From the trailhead, follow the main park trail and look for the spur marked for climbing access, which leads to the peak from the east. Another way is to take the wide cart path from the visitor center to the first climbers' trail sign, then head up and left toward the peak.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Shares its start with Birthday Party

name: Pedrick's Chimney
beta: Start at the highest point of the upper talus and climb the easy wide dihedral, trending left, to the base of the chimney. Follow the chimney, passing a bolt, to a broad ledge, then scramble up the gullies to the south and west to the summit.
overview: A very easy line on the Gargoyle Wall, up a wide dihedral and a chimney to a broad ledge, with scrambling beyond to reach the summit of the Head.

current.descent: rap 27 m from the eyebolt
current.location: Highest point of the upper talus
